steps.do: In the program menu, click Documents.
steps.see: One list of 30 documents under tabs: All, Plans, Policies, Categorization, Agreements. One needs-attention card.
steps.was: Plans, Policies and the ITCSC were three pages under two menu groups.

steps.do: Click the System security plan row.
steps.see: The editor opens at once. Its way back, top left, says Documents.
steps.was: A side preview opened; the editor was one more click behind its arrow.

steps.do: Click in AC-1's narrative, type a sentence, click outside it.
steps.see: Saved to AC-1's implementation: the control's page reads the same text.
steps.was: The same editor, six clicks from the menu.

steps.see: Mission Computer's Software & firmware, with a bar at the foot: Back to SSP section 8.
steps.was: Open record went to the read-only Inventory, with no way back.

steps.do: Click Add item, add a firmware, then click Back to SSP section 8.
steps.see: Section 8, at Mission Computer's row, now prints the firmware you added.
steps.was: Firmware could not be added, and section 8 was a fixed table.

steps.do: Go back to Documents. On the card, click Placeholder narratives.
steps.see: The editor opens on the first placeholder narrative, the cursor in it.
steps.was: Every link to the SSP landed at its top.

steps.do: Click New document, keep A blank plan, type a title, Create document.
steps.see: The new plan opens as a draft to write in, and is listed on Documents.
steps.was: New plan offered three templates on the Plans page.

walks.title: A requirement, from creation to evidence

steps.do: Click Create requirement. Give a title and a statement, type AC-2 under Maps control, tick Mission Computer, create.
steps.see: The new requirement's own page: AC-2 under Controls, Mission Computer under Components.
steps.was: The dialog closed with a message; nothing was created.

steps.do: Click in the statement, add a sentence, click outside it.
steps.see: The line under it says it is saved to the requirement.
steps.was: A requirement's statement could not be edited from its preview.

steps.do: Under Components click Allocate, search Secure Boot, tick it, allocate.
steps.see: Components 2. Secure Boot Controller's Requirements tab lists it too.
steps.was: A requirement could not be allocated to a component.

steps.do: Under Evidence click Link evidence, search Destruction, tick it, link.
steps.see: Evidence 1. The picker searched all 368 artifacts.
steps.was: Link evidence offered six artifacts in a drop-down.

steps.do: Link evidence again; click Add evidence at the top; give it a title; add.
steps.see: A new artifact, waiting on review, linked here and listed on Evidence.
steps.was: There was no way to add an artifact while linking.

steps.do: Go back by the breadcrumb. Point at the first row and click its eye.
steps.see: The row shows AC-2, two components, two artifacts; the eye previews it beside the list.
steps.was: The preview was the only view of a requirement.

steps.do: Open Evidence. In the view menu choose Waiting on review, click a row's eye, then Accept.
steps.see: The view counts one less; a requirement that stood on it alone reads Supported.
steps.was: The register listed 6 of 368; a review was a dialog elsewhere.

steps.see: The requirement you created is under its Requirements.
steps.was: Each page kept its own list of requirements.

open: The base registers (640 requirements, 368 artifacts) are the workbook's records, read by calling PA.sctm.build() (about 80 ms) on the first draw and after anything the chain changed.
17 requirements read No control mapped and 598 Not allocated: that is the snapshot (it holds components for 42 requirements), now visible as chips.
The three plans v2 listed among the policies (IR-8, CP-2, CM-9) are folded into their plan rows, so Policies counts 18, not 21.
STIG checklists (7) sit in the kinds switch beside All evidence 368 but are not part of the 368: fact(evidence) is unchanged.
The customer's document rows open v2's read-only preview (v7p-creq): its answers are not editable here.
Policies, the three plans' editors, the ITCSC and a checklist's page are v2's pages in v2's look; only their way back was renamed.
A primary button in a preview draws as a plain button (v2's layer); on the record's page it is the primary.
Unmapping a control the snapshot mapped is kept in ctl.unmap: the workbook and v2's own pages do not follow. Evidence linked here (req.evl) is not in the workbook either.

SSP: sections 5, 6, 7 and 9 are fixed tables; only section 8 gains rows and software lines from System, section 10 one line from Controls, section 11 the per-component text. AC-2's narrative is locked by v2's scripted AI draft until it is accepted or rejected.
SSP narratives are kept in PA.SSP in memory, as the editor always did: a reload of the file forgets them (requirements, evidence and documents made here survive it).
New document's templates are lane X's three; their keys are written in this module. A blank document has no version history.
fact(requirements).total is now the highest requirement number in use (count is the rows), so the lanes number the next requirement without colliding.
Renew by is not in the snapshot: Expiring shows only after a date is set here.
A created program: the three registers draw lane P's records in the kit's table with lane P's own dialogs and previews; the requirement's page is WS-X90 only.
After Create requirement the reader lands on the new requirement's page (not the register); a link sent with PA.v2.go('requirements', { open }) lands there too.
Not walked at 390 beyond the route checks: the flows were driven at 1440.

Found by the re-walk, not fixed: a requirement created on a component reads "Created today on the Requirements register" and its number can skip (REQ-644 after 640); Link evidence's button reads "Link 1 artifact".
Pass 3, not done: views.mjs prints 3 failed on each list because of the seeded saved view (see checks.views); the script is the lead's.

Pass 3: a part of a list's question that has no control in the mode shown (Gap, Component and Family on the customer's document; Answer elsewhere; Review and Owner on STIG checklists) is passed to K.toolbar as a filter the lane's CSS hides (acts k3d.h.*), so a saved view picked from any mode asks its whole question. The kit has no hidden filter of its own.

Pass 3: a question another page sent (requirements chosen elsewhere, the requirements that map a control) is a note over the row with Show every requirement, not a control of the row; a saved view does not keep it, and Clear or any view ends it.

Pass 3: a document's preview (k3d-doc) lists the SSP's sections, placeholder narratives and revisions, a plan's sections, the evidence its text cites and its revision, the ITCSC's versions. A policy's preview has its facts and its revision only: its page's Versions, Objectives, Comments and History are v2's. A plan's cited evidence rows are plain text: their titles match no artifact of the register.
Pass 3: Remediation rows on a requirement open v2's POA&M preview (no V3 record kind for them); STIG checklist rows and the customer document's rows go to v2's page or preview and have no eye.

Pass 3, the kit's and not changed: on a phone a list's name column is cut to about 24 characters (its 220px minimum); a record page's header stacks its two actions beside a long title (an artifact's page).
Pass 3: the walks and shots entries of this file still say tabs and chips (pass 2's words); the walk itself is current.
Pass 3: Evidence shows Renew by as a column only while a row on the page has a date (the snapshot records none).
